blocks.text: Where a medical writer's day goes

No public time study ranks the tasks medical writers do. The research behind this page looked and did not find one. No source says which computer tasks take the most hours for medical writers. What you get instead is the job description and the tool data. That is enough to see the shape of the day.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics describes technical writers, the closest group it covers. Their duties include writing or revising content, editing material from other writers, standardizing content across platforms, and collecting user feedback to update it. Medical writing is a different field with its own rules. The same kinds of work still show up in your week.

The BLS also says technical writers may be expected to work evenings and weekends to meet deadlines. Review cycles and submission dates can bring the same squeeze. When a deadline moves, the evening work lands on the drafting hours, not on the email.
Four kinds of work that fill the hours

items: Drafting and revising sections. This is the block you protect, and it is where interruptions do the most damage.
Editing text from other writers, statisticians and clinicians. You spend time on tone, consistency and sources you did not write.
Standardizing terms, units and headings across documents. These drift when several people touch the same file.
Email, chat and reviewer comments. The research cannot size these hours for medical writers, so log them yourself.

blocks.text: Why email and interruptions eat the afternoon

Microsoft's June 2025 Work Trend Index covered 31,000 knowledge workers in 31 markets. It found the average employee receives 117 emails and 153 Teams messages a day. Employees are interrupted 275 times a day by meetings, emails or chat notifications. Those numbers count messages and interruptions. They do not say how many minutes each one costs.

An older McKinsey estimate is more direct. A 2012 report put the time that interaction workers spend managing email at about 28% of the workweek. That is a different group, and the figure comes from a blog summary. The original report was not checked directly. Treat it as a rough marker, not a medical writer figure.

A 2020 time study of physicians found 7.7% of office time went to administrative activities. It is a different job, and it does not separate email. Use it only as a comparison point for how much admin work a professional can absorb.

blocks.title: Measure one week first
blocks.text: Log every email and chat block for one working week. Write the start time, the length and what each one was for. Your own log will tell you more than any survey about your day.
Tool sprawl: reference software, PDFs and time tracking

A 2024 survey of freelance medical communicators, published in the AMWA Journal in March 2025, had 291 participants. Of those, 74% used citation or reference management software. 57% did not use time-tracking software, and 51% did not use accounting software. The survey covered mostly freelance writers, so it is not a clean picture of an employed pharma team.

The AMWA blog summary of the same survey gives different numbers. It says 65% use reference software and that EndNote is the most common tool among those users. It also names Adobe Acrobat as the most frequently recommended tool, at 80%. The two AMWA sources disagree on the reference software figure. Check the journal article before you quote either number.

The lesson holds even with the mixed numbers. Your references, PDFs, time logs and documents live in several places. Each switch costs attention. Pick one place to keep your source list, and link everything else back to it.
How an AI assistant for medical writers fits your Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch of your Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything on screen. It points at things, draws a circle and a label around them, and answers out loud. It does not click buttons, edit files or run other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Word.

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. You can add snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. For medical writing, the personal dictionary is the feature to set up first. Drug names, abbreviations and sponsor product codes go in once and stay put.
The same pattern works in Pages and in Google Docs in a browser. Hold ⌥⌘ over the document and ask. Lazur sees what is on screen, so close windows that show data you should not share before you ask.

items: 'Where is Compare?' Lazur circles the button and labels it. You click it.
'Walk me through turning off Track Changes for the final copy.' Lazur waits after each click.
'Explain this sentence in the protocol.' Lazur answers out loud from what is on screen.
'Draft a note asking the statistician for the revised tables.' Lazur drafts the text, and you read it before it goes out.

blocks.text: Worked example: comparing two versions of a results section in Word

A statistician sends a revised results section as a separate file. You have your own edited copy open. You need to see every change before you merge them. In Word for Mac, open the newer file, then go to Review > Compare > Compare. Pick the older file as the original and the newer one as the revised document.

Word opens a comparison window with a list of changes. If you lose track of where the changes panel went, hold ⌥⌘ and ask. Lazur circles the control, and you click it yourself. It will not click for you, so you stay in control of every merge.

Three traps catch people. Check which file is marked as original before you accept anything. Two files with similar names are easy to mix up. Read the merged result once, from top to bottom, before you send it to the reviewer. A quick read catches a changed unit or a dropped footnote that a list of changes can hide.
Dictation for drug names, units and boilerplate

Dictation is fast for first drafts. It is weaker on unusual words. Drug names, device names and abbreviations are where a dictation tool slips. Put your list in the personal dictionary before a long session. Then read every drug name, dose and number by eye.

blocks.title: Numbers need a human check
blocks.text: Dictation can turn a dose, a confidence interval or a p-value into something close but wrong. Read each number against the source table before it leaves your hands.

Snippets help with text you type every week, such as a standard safety statement or a title page block. Clipboard slots hold reference text while you write, so you switch windows less often. To check how accurate your dictation is on your own voice, try the [dictation accuracy checker](/tools/dictation-accuracy-checker).
Confidential trial data and your employer's rules

Medical writers often see unpublished results, sponsor material and sometimes patient-level detail. Your employer sets the rules for what can go into an AI tool. Follow them. Ask your compliance or legal team before you use any AI tool on confidential material.

Here is what Lazur does with your data. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot are sent to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. This page does not claim any compliance certification, and it is not legal advice.

items: Check your employer's policy on AI tools and on the type of document.
Close other windows that show data you are not allowed to share.
Use public or internal drafts first, so you learn how Lazur answers.
Never screenshot or read aloud patient identifiers.

blocks.text: Common mistakes medical writers make with AI tools

items: Trusting a summary without checking the source. Read the paragraph Lazur points to.
Accepting a reference the tool wrote. Find each citation in the original paper.
Dictating drug names and doses without a read-through.
Forgetting what is on screen. Anything visible can be seen while you hold the key.
Using one tool for every task. Keep the source document as the final authority.

blocks.text: A quieter mistake is skipping the time log. Without one, you cannot tell whether a tool saved you an hour or only moved the work around. Note the task, the start time and the tool before you decide what stays.

faq.question: Is Lazur a plugin for Microsoft Word?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Word, Pages or any other app. It is a voice assistant on your Mac. It sees the screen while you hold ⌥⌘, points at controls, and answers out loud. It does not click or edit for you.

faq.question: Can Lazur write my citations for me?
faq.answer: It can draft text, but do not trust a reference it writes. Find each citation in the original source, check the authors, year and page, and only then keep it. Treat every reference as unverified until you have opened the paper.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on confidential trial data?
faq.answer: Check your employer's rules first. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot are sent to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. This page does not claim any compliance certification, so ask your compliance team.

faq.question: Which Macs does Lazur run on?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Check the download page for the current requirements before you install.

faq.answer: There is a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, with 150 AI actions. Power is $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both.

faq.question: Does dictation work in Word and Pages?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Read the output before you save. Use the personal dictionary for drug names and abbreviations. Lazur does not click for you, so you still place the cursor.

faq.question: Which Mac versions do Word and Pages need?
faq.answer: The Mac App Store listing for Word says it requires macOS 14.0 or later. Pages 15.4 requires macOS 26 or later. Check each app before you upgrade your Mac, because the two requirements differ.

faq.question: Does Lazur replace a medical writer's judgment?
faq.answer: No. Lazur helps you find controls, explain text on screen, dictate and draft. Decisions about claims, data and sign-off stay with you and your team.
